title: SKIF explosion chamber process observation demo
origin: SKIF explosion chamber: experimental observation of a metal sample under shock loading.

tension.description: Shock loading of a metallic sample and subsequent structural degradation.
tension.observed_change: Growth of internal stress followed by local rupture and loss of structural connectivity.
tension.research_question: At what moment does the sample transition from reversible deformation to irreversible structural damage?

description: Demo ODF event for illustrating how multiple experimental data streams can be connected to one observed process rather than stored as isolated files.

signals.description: Time-resolved X-ray image sequence of the sample during shock loading.
High-speed optical video of external deformation and visible fracture development.
Pressure profile of the shock wave during the experiment.
Local strain measurements from the sample surface and fixture points.

invariants.name: sample
invariants.description: Material sample identity preserved across all data streams.

invariants.name: facility
invariants.description: Experimental facility where the event is observed.

invariants.name: experiment_series
invariants.description: Experimental series identifier linking related tests.

invariants.name: shared_timebase
invariants.description: Common temporal frame used to connect signals from different instruments.

ruptures.description: First visible local damage zone appears in the sample structure.
Loss of structural connectivity becomes observable across multiple signals.

interpretation.description: The event is interpreted as a shock-induced structural transition: a process in which accumulated internal stress produces local damage, followed by loss of connectivity in the material structure.

notes: ODF demo principle: the experiment is represented as one process event, not as a folder of disconnected files.
Each signal preserves its origin through EVENT_SKIF_EXPLOSION_001 and remains linked to tension, invariants and ruptures.
